papers.title: Mechanical Performance and Energy Absorption of Ti6Al4V I-WP Lattice Metamaterials Manufactured via Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Metamaterial lattice structures based on a Triply Periodic Minimal Surface (TPMS) structure have attracted much attention due to their excellent mechanical properties and energy absorption capabilities. In this study, a novel TPMS lattice metamaterial structure (IWP-X) is designed to enhance the axial mechanical properties by fusing an X-shaped plate with an IWP surface structure. A selective laser melting (SLM) machine was utilized to print the designed lattice structures with Ti6Al4V powder. The thickness of the plate and the density of the IWP are varied to explore the responsivity of the mechanical and energy absorption properties with the volume ratio of IWP-X. The finite element simulation analysis is used to effectively predict the stress distribution and fracture site of each structure in the compression test. The results show that the IWP-X structure obtains the ultimate compressive strength of 122.06% improvement, and the energy absorption of 282.03% improvement. The specific energy absorption (SEA) reaches its maximum value in the plate-to-IWP volume ratio of 0.7 to 0.8.

llm.relevance_to_user: 论文研究Ti6Al4V I-WP点阵结构的力学性能与能量吸收，虽不直接涉及股骨柄设计，但点阵结构设计方法可能为多孔股骨柄提供借鉴。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not address femoral stem design, implant mechanics, or any biomedical context; it focuses on generic lattice metamaterial performance without application to orthopaedic implants.

summary_zh.motivation: 提升三周期极小曲面点阵结构的力学性能与能量吸收能力。
summary_zh.method: 将X形板与IWP表面结构融合设计新型IWP-X点阵，改变板厚与密度并通过SLM制备。
summary_zh.result: IWP-X结构抗压强度提升122.06%，能量吸收提升282.03%，比吸能在板与IWP体积比0.7-0.8时最大。
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩实验与有限元模拟验证力学性能与断裂位置。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance the mechanical properties and energy absorption of TPMS lattice structures for potential structural applications.
summary_en.method: A novel IWP-X lattice metamaterial was designed by fusing an X-shaped plate with an IWP surface, fabricated via selective laser melting in Ti6Al4V with varying plate thickness and density.
summary_en.result: The IWP-X structure achieved a 122.06% improvement in ultimate compressive strength and a 282.03% improvement in energy absorption, with maximum specific energy absorption at a plate-to-IWP volume ratio of 0.7–0.8.
summary_en.validation: Experimental compression tests and finite element simulations validated the stress distribution and fracture locations of the lattice structures.
